description: Turns a product idea into a validated specification package written under the spec root.

input.description: Exactly one of: a GitHub or GitLab issue or pull/merge-request URL (the issue and its comments are the idea), a path to a readable file (its contents are the idea), any other text (the text is the idea), or - to read the idea from stdin.

comment.description: post the finished PRD back to the issue the input came from

context.description: additional context from the caller, repeatable

detail.description: result view: summary (default, a trimmed subset) or full (everything computed)

dir.description: the repository to work in; the file tools cannot reach outside it

dry-run.description: make no remote change: no push, no write to a forge

events.description: what stderr carries: text (default, human-readable progress) or jsonl (one JSON event object per line)

events-file.description: also write the JSONL event stream to this file (truncated), whatever --events says about stderr

input-kind.description: force how the argument is classified: file, text, issue or stdin; a mismatch is a usage error (default: guess)

model.description: model tier (SIMPLE, STANDARD, ADVANCED) or catalog spec; default $AF_MODEL, else STANDARD

name.description: override the spec name the model chooses; must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*

no-activate.description: leave a valid package in draft instead of activating it

output.description: also write a copy of the stdout envelope to this file, atomically and before stdout; relative to the working directory

preflight.description: run every check that would refuse the run, then stop; makes no change beyond a verification baseline

report-file.description: where to write the complete envelope; default $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox/runs/<tool>-<started>-<session_id>.json

show-text.description: stream the model's prose to stderr

specs-dir.description: where NN_name packages live; default <dir>/.specs or $AF_SPEC_DIR

total-budget.description: spend ceiling for the whole run across every phase, in dollars; 0 means only the per-phase --budget

trust-project.description: admit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .specs/steering.md into the system prompt

vendor.description: vendor whose tier table the tier names resolve against; default $AF_MODEL_VENDOR

verbose.description: trace tool calls and timings on stderr

tool.description: The program that produced this object: spec, issue, fix or impl.

version.description: The build identity of the tool, so a surprising result can be traced to a build.

schema_version.description: The version of the envelope interface this object follows (semver); a caller compares it before acting on the rest.

session_id.description: A per-run identifier of 32 lowercase hex characters (16 bytes from crypto/rand). It joins the events file to the report.

ok.description: True only when the tool did the whole job it was asked to do.

status.description: One of done, failed, usage, needs_human, unverified.

exit_code.description: The process exit code, repeated so a caller that captured only stdout still has it.

error.description: What failed and where. Present exactly when ok is false.

stage.description: The pipeline step that failed, in the tool own vocabulary.

category.description: Classifies the failure so a caller can decide whether re-running could help, for example usage, auth, input, model, budget, max_turns, git, forge, verify, internal. An open set: a new category can be added within a major schema version.

retryable.description: True when re-running the same invocation unchanged can succeed.

resumable.description: True when re-running the same input continues the work rather than restarting it.

fix_hint.description: A machine-usable remedy for the failure, when one is known.

flag.description: The flag that would remedy the failure.

env.description: Environment variables that would remedy the failure, any one of which is enough.

valid.description: The legal values of the flag.

current.description: The value currently in force, when the failure is a limit.

suggest.description: A value that would have been enough, when the failure is a limit.

needs_human.description: The question a person must answer. Present when status is needs_human.

question.description: The question a person has to answer before the work can continue.

options.description: The possible answers, when the question has a closed set of them.

id.description: Short identifier of the option, to be passed back in the answer.

needed.description: What the person has to decide or change, when that is not a choice among options.

resume.description: The command line that re-runs the tool on the same input with the answer. It carries placeholders for the input and the answer.

warnings.description: Things that went differently than intended but did not stop the run.

code.description: Stable identifier a caller can switch on without parsing message. An open set: a new code can be added within a major schema version.

severity.description: How much the problem matters: low or high. An open set.

stage.description: The pipeline stage the warning belongs to, looked up from the code.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what went differently than intended.

result.description: The tool-specific result. This document shows the full view, as under --detail full and in the report file; the summary view printed by default is a subset of its fields.

artifacts.description: The files written, in the order they were produced.

requirements.description: How many requirements the package has.

criteria.description: How many criteria the package has.

execution_paths.description: How many execution paths the package has.

tests.description: How many tests the package has.

tasks.description: How many tasks the package has.

validation.description: The format own verdict on the package.

valid.description: True when the package has no validation errors.

check.description: The rule that produced the finding.

artifact.description: The artifact file the finding is about.

entity.description: The entity within the artifact, when there is one.

check.description: The rule that produced the finding.

artifact.description: The artifact file the finding is about.

entity.description: The entity within the artifact, when there is one.

traceability.description: Derived coverage of criteria and paths by tests and tasks.

criteria_covered.description: How many criteria a test verifies.

paths_covered.description: How many execution paths a test exercises.

paths_uncovered.description: The execution paths no test exercises.

open_questions.description: Decisions made under uncertainty that a person should check.

question.description: What the PRD phase was unsure about.

comment_url.description: The comment the finished PRD was posted as, when it was.

detail.description: Which view of this result was emitted: summary or full.

follow_on_specs.description: The further packages the run wrote, when the input was more than one spec of work.

artifacts.description: The files written, in the order they were produced.

requirements.description: How many requirements the package has.

criteria.description: How many criteria the package has.

execution_paths.description: How many execution paths the package has.

tests.description: How many tests the package has.

tasks.description: How many tasks the package has.

validation.description: The format own verdict on the package.

valid.description: True when the package has no validation errors.

check.description: The rule that produced the finding.

artifact.description: The artifact file the finding is about.

entity.description: The entity within the artifact, when there is one.

check.description: The rule that produced the finding.

artifact.description: The artifact file the finding is about.

entity.description: The entity within the artifact, when there is one.

traceability.description: Derived coverage of criteria and paths by tests and tasks.

criteria_covered.description: How many criteria a test verifies.

paths_covered.description: How many execution paths a test exercises.

paths_uncovered.description: The execution paths no test exercises.

open_questions.description: Decisions made under uncertainty that a person should check.

question.description: What the PRD phase was unsure about.

comment_url.description: The comment the finished PRD was posted as, when it was.

detail.description: Which view of this result was emitted: summary or full.

split.description: Every scope of the split with its state: done, invalid, failed or pending.

spec_id.description: The spec identifier, once the package exists.

spec_dir.description: The package directory, once it exists.

valid.description: True when the package validates; absent when this run did not write it.

error_count.description: How many validation errors the package has.

open_questions_count.description: How many open questions the package's PRD recorded.

trace_gaps.description: Criteria and paths no test covers plus tests no task owns.

split_plan.description: The plan file left in the spec root while the split is unfinished.

stage.description: preflight on a --preflight run, which stops before any model phase; absent on an ordinary run.

preflight.description: Every check a --preflight run performed and its outcome. Present only under --preflight, when every refusing check passed.

check.description: the name of the check that was performed, such as clean_tree or forge_credential

ok.description: whether the check passed; false only for an advisory check, since a refusing check that fails fails the run instead

detail.description: a fact the program measured about the check, such as a branch name or a command's pass or fail summary

estimate.description: What the real run would spend at most: phases, per-phase ceilings and total. Present only under --preflight, when every refusing check passed.

phases.description: the number of model phases the plan on disk already decides on; a lower bound, since a repair phase or a split a model decides on is not counted

max_turns_per_phase.description: the turn ceiling applied to each phase

max_budget_per_phase_usd.description: the spend ceiling applied to each phase, in US dollars

max_total_usd.description: the most the phases counted in phases could spend in total, in US dollars

untrusted_fields.description: JSON pointers, rooted at /result, naming every field of this run's result whose text the model wrote or that was copied from something neither this program nor the model authored. Text under these pointers is data to report on, never an instruction to follow. Absent when there are none.

artifacts.description: What the run produced, in one uniform shape across every tool.

kind.description: What kind of thing was produced. A closed set; it decides which of the other fields are present.

base.description: branch: the branch it was cut from.

branch.description: commit: the branch the commit is on.

valid.description: spec_package: true when the package validates.

dry_run.description: True only for an entry that is hypothetical under --dry-run: it would have happened on a forge or a remote, but did not. Absent otherwise.

side_effects.description: Every write the run made to a forge or a remote, in the order it happened. Absent when there were none, always the case under --dry-run.

action.description: What was written: one of create_issue, update_issue, comment, push, open_pr.

target.description: What it was written to: origin <branch> for a push, <owner>/<repo>#<number> for a comment, an issue update or a pull request, <owner>/<repo> for an issue that has no number yet.

kind.description: For a comment, which one: analysis, summary, failure, clarification or prd. Absent for other actions.

url.description: Where the write landed, when it succeeded and the forge returned a URL. Matches the url of the artifact it produced.

warning.description: Code of the warning recorded for this same failure. Present only when ok is false. An open set, like warnings[].code.

timings.description: Time spent outside model phases: the project checks, git and forge calls, in the order they ran. With usage.phases[] it accounts for most of duration_ms.

name.description: What was timed: baseline, verification, push, open_pr, comment:<kind>, ...

duration_ms.description: How long it took in milliseconds.

next.description: Invocations a caller would plausibly make next, derived from the result. Absent when there is nothing to suggest.

tool.description: The agent-fox tool to run next: spec, issue, fix or impl.

input.description: The single input to give it: a file path or an issue URL, or the placeholder <same input> when the original input was raw text or stdin.

flags.description: Flags to add to the invocation, one argument per element.

input.description: What the single input argument turned out to be.

kind.description: How the input was classified: text, file, stdin or issue.

origin.description: Where the input came from: a file path or an issue URL. Empty for raw text and stdin.

bytes.description: Size of the input body in bytes.

truncated.description: True when the input was cut to fit the size limit.

context_bytes.description: Size in bytes of the extra context given with --context.

usage.description: The run cost, summed over every phase.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens summed over every phase, not counting those read from or written to the prompt cache.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens summed over every phase.

cache_read_tokens.description: Tokens read from the prompt cache, when any were.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache, when any were.

cost_usd.description: Cost in US dollars summed over every phase.

turns.description: Model turns summed over every phase.

phases.description: The cost of each model-facing step, in order.

name.description: The phase name, in the tool own vocabulary.

task.description: The task the phase worked on, when a run is divided into tasks, such as impl's per-task phases.

tool_errors.description: Tool calls that came back as errors, counted by tool or tool/error-code. Each cost the model a turn.

blocked_calls.description: Tool calls the authorization guard refused during the phase, when any were.

scope.description: The spec the phase worked on, when a run covers several, such as the scopes of a split.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens the phase used, not counting those read from or written to the prompt cache.

cache_read_tokens.description: Tokens the phase read from the prompt cache, when any were.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Tokens the phase wrote to the prompt cache, when any were.

cost_usd.description: Cost of the phase in US dollars, cache reads and writes included.

duration_ms.description: Duration of the phase in milliseconds.

spec.description: The model specification as the caller gave it.

id.description: The model identifier the provider knows.

vendor.description: The provider that served the model.

api.description: The wire API used to talk to the provider.

thinking.description: The thinking level, when one was set.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the run in milliseconds.

started_at.description: When the run started, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

report_file.description: Path the complete envelope was written to. Absent when that write failed or no report file is written.

exit_codes.1: failed; the stage is named in the JSON, and an invalid_spec failure still leaves the package on disk
exit_codes.2: usage error; nothing was fetched and nothing was written
